docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Use Register Project from the left sidebar. The project is the top-level IMDA record and must be created before a study can be registered.

Temporary Project ID

After submitting this form, IMDA will assign a temporary Project ID in the format TEMP_IMP_XX.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Official name of the overall research project. Use a specific, descriptive title. Do not use only a disease, organism, or instrument name. Project Contributors* Principal Investigator, submitter, and other people responsible for the project. Enter full names and use valid email addresses and complete institution names wherever requested. Research Area* Main scientific subject area of the project. Select the closest available controlled term. If no suitable term exists, check Browse Lists or request an addition through Update List. Funding Source* Funding agency, grant number, or institutional support. Use the official funder name and grant number. If there was no external funding, follow the option provided by IMDA. Project Description* Brief description of the project purpose, scope, and expected data. Write 3-5 clear sentences that explain the research question and the type of metabolomics work.

docs.title: Submit and Continue
docs.text:
1. Fill all fields marked with an asterisk.
  2. Select the closest Research Area.
  3. Check the funding source and project description carefully.
  4. Click Submit to register the project.
  5. Keep the temporary Project ID and select it when registering the study.
Next: Study ↓

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text: Use this checklist to prepare the metadata and data files required for an IMDA submission. Preparing these details in advance helps prevent missing information, incorrect file links, and repeated uploads.

docs.title: Complete Submission Flow
docs.text:
The flowchart gives a quick overview of the complete submission. Keep it on this page as a reference, then use the sections in the left navigation for detailed instructions.

Temporary and Permanent IDs

During the submission process, IMDA provides temporary identifiers:

  • Project: TEMP_IMP_XX
  • Study: TEMP_IMS_XX

After the submission is completed, IMDA assigns permanent accession IDs:

  • Project accession: IMP_XXXXXX
  • Study accession: IMS_XXXXXX

docs.title: How IMDA Records Are Connected
docs.text:
IMDA records information in linked stages. Complete each stage before moving to the next one.

IMDA Section What It Describes Record Link Project The overall research activity and its contributors, research area, funding, and purpose. One project can contain multiple studies. Study A specific investigation or dataset within the project, including its title, design, summary, authors, and release information. Every study belongs to one project. Sample The biological or other source material used in the study, including sample characteristics and experimental conditions. Every sample belongs to one study. Experiment The analytical assay used to measure the samples, such as mass spectrometry (MS) or nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Experiment rows connect Sample IDs to data files. Data files Raw or processed files produced by the instrument, together with their file names and MD5 checksums. Every file must match an experiment-template row.

docs.title: Account and Contributor Details
docs.text:
• Keep the submitter's active email address, full name, organization, designation, country, and ORCID ready.
  • Collect the full names, email addresses, affiliations, and roles of the Principal Investigator and contributing authors.
  • Make sure the user profile identifies the person responsible for the submission.

docs.title: Project and Study Description
docs.text:
• Prepare a clear project title, project description, research area, funding agency, and grant number where applicable.
  • Prepare a descriptive study title, a short scientific summary, study type, data type, keywords, and release date.
  • Keep publication identifiers and ethical or institutional approval numbers ready where applicable.
  • Use consistent project, study, method, and author information throughout the submission.

docs.title: Sample Metadata
docs.text:
• Prepare a unique name for every sample, including controls, standards, pooled samples, and quality-control samples where used.
  • Record the sample source, scientific organism name, taxonomy ID, sample type, preparation and extraction methods, experimental condition, treatment time, replicate information, and storage conditions.
  • Record the exact number of data files belonging to each sample.
  • Download and complete the sample template in the Sample section. Do not change its column names or order.

docs.title: Experiment and Data Files
docs.text:
• Decide whether the experiment uses MS or NMR and prepare the instrument, acquisition, and data-processing details.
  • Keep the final raw data and processed/result files ready. Compress each complex raw-data folder into its own ZIP file.
  • Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and dots in file and folder names. Do not use spaces or special characters.
  • Use open data formats where available, such as mzML for MS and nmrML for NMR.
  • Install an FTP client such as FileZilla for data-file upload.
  • Download the relevant MS or NMR template in the Experiment section after IMDA has generated the Sample IDs.

docs.title: Keep Names and IDs Consistent
docs.text:
The same information is reused across several stages. A mismatch can prevent file mapping or validation.

Information Consistency Rule Project ID Select the correct project when registering the study. Study ID Use the same study when registering samples, experiments, and FTP files. Sample ID Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID into the first column of the MS or NMR template. Sample name Use the same unique sample name in the sample and experiment templates. Data-file name Enter the exact final file name, including its extension, in the experiment template. MD5 checksum Generate it from the final file or ZIP and enter the matching value in the same experiment row.

Use NA When Information Is Unavailable

Throughout the IMDA submission, enter NA in a metadata-template cell or free-text field when the requested information is genuinely not available or not applicable. Do not leave such cells blank. Do not use NA instead of an IMDA-generated ID, a required dropdown selection, a compulsory file, or mandatory account and contact information.

Before Moving Ahead

Complete Project, Study, and Sample registration before preparing the final experiment template. Finalize each data file and calculate its MD5 checksum before registering the experiment. Do not rename, edit, or recompress a file after calculating its checksum.

Next: Login / Register ↓

docs.title: Experiment
docs.text: Use Register Experiment from the left sidebar after registering samples and calculating the MD5 checksum for every final data file. Select the technique and Study ID, then upload the result file and completed MS or NMR template.

docs.title: What to Fill in the Portal
docs.text: Portal Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Select Technique* Select the experiment technique, such as MS or NMR. Choose the same technique used in the study and template. Study Select the Study ID linked to this experiment. Make sure the selected study belongs to the correct project. Metabolite / Compound File* Upload the processed metabolite/compound identification or quantification result file. This file is compulsory. Use a clear file name. Do not use this field for the raw instrument data uploaded later through FTP. MS/NMR File Template Upload the completed MS or NMR Excel template. Use MS template for mass spectrometry and NMR template for nuclear magnetic resonance. Do not change column headers.

docs.title: Where to Get Sample IDs
docs.text:
After sample registration, open My Sample to view the generated Sample ID values. Copy these IDs into the first column, Sample id, of the MS or NMR experiment template.

Sample ID Rule

Do not enter a local sample name in the Sample id column. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID exactly as shown in My Sample. If one sample has multiple data files, repeat that Sample ID once for each file row. For example, if Sample ID 1060 has two files, enter 1060 in two rows and provide the matching file name and checksum in each row.

Do Not Change Column Headers

Do not rename, delete, move, or reorder any column header in the Sample, MS, or NMR templates. Fill the templates using the original column names and order supplied by IMDA.

docs.title: MS Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the MS file template when the study uses mass spectrometry. Fill one row for each sample-and-file combination.

Use Dropdown Values

In the MS template, columns such as Mass Spectrometer Type, MS Instrument Name, MS Instrument Type, MS Ionization Method, and Ion Mode/Scan Polarity have dropdown options. Select the closest correct value from the dropdown. Use Others only when the correct instrument or method is not available in the list.

MS Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample id First column in the MS template. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID from My Sample exactly. Sample Name Sample name used in the sample template. Reference Standard Reference or internal standard used during the assay. Enter NA only if it does not apply. Chromatography Instrument Name LC/GC/CE or other chromatography system used before MS. Column Model Chromatography column model/name. Column Type Column chemistry/type, such as C18, HILIC, GC column, or NA. Mass Spectrometer Type Select from the dropdown, such as LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS, MALDI-TOF, Tandem MS, or the closest available type. MS Instrument Name Select the instrument model/name from the dropdown list. Example options include ABI Sciex, Agilent, Bruker, Thermo, Waters, Shimadzu, and other instrument entries. MS Instrument Type Select from the dropdown, such as Triple TOF, TOF, QTOF, Orbitrap, FT-ICR-MS, Single quadrupole, Triple quadrupole, or Others. MS Ionization Method Select from the dropdown, such as ESI, nano ESI, APCI, APPI, MALDI, EI, CI, FAB, DIOS, or Others. Ion Mode/Scan Polarity Select from the dropdown: Positive, Negative, or Positive;Negative. Data Transformation(Software/s Used) Software used to convert or process the data, such as ProteoWizard, XCMS, MZmine, vendor software, or NA. MS Data File Name Exact raw or ZIP data-file name that will be uploaded through FTP. Include the extension. Md5checksum MD5 checksum for the final uploaded MS data file. Generate it after the ZIP/file is final.

Multiple Files for One Sample

If Number of files per sample is 2, create 2 rows for that sample in the MS template. Repeat the same Sample id and enter the matching MS Data File Name and Md5checksum for each file.

docs.title: NMR Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the NMR file template when the study uses nuclear magnetic resonance. Fill one row for each sample-and-file combination.

Use Dropdown Values

In the NMR template, columns such as NMR Instrument Name, NMR Type, NMR Experiment Type, and NMR Solvent have dropdown options. Select the closest correct value from the dropdown. Use Others only when the correct solvent or option is not available in the list.

NMR Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample id First column in the NMR template. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID from My Sample exactly. Sample Name Sample name used in the sample template. Reference Standard Reference standard used for NMR. Enter NA if not applicable. NMR Instrument Name Select the instrument model/name from the dropdown list. Example options include Bruker and Jeol NMR instrument entries. NMR Type Select from the dropdown: Solution NMR or Solid State NMR. NMR Experiment Type Select from the dropdown, such as 1D 1H, 1D 13C, 1D 31P, 2D experiments, or the closest available option. NMR Spectrometer Frequency Spectrometer frequency, such as 400 MHz, 500 MHz, or 600 MHz. NMR Probe Probe used for acquisition. NMR Probe Temperature Probe/sample temperature during acquisition, with unit where possible. NMR Solvent Select from the dropdown, such as CCL4, CS2, CDCL3, C6D6, D2O, Acetone, DMSO, Methanol, Ethanol, or Others. NMR Tube Size Tube size, such as 5 mm, or NA if not applicable. Data Transformation(Software/s Used) Software used for processing/conversion. NMR Data File Name Exact raw or ZIP NMR data-file name that will be uploaded through FTP. Include the extension. Md5checksum MD5 checksum for the final uploaded NMR data file. Generate it after the ZIP/file is final.

Multiple Files for One Sample

If Number of files per sample is 2, create 2 rows for that sample in the NMR template. Repeat the same Sample id and enter the matching NMR Data File Name and Md5checksum for each file.

docs.title: Match Samples, Files, and Checksums
docs.text:
1. Use the Sample IDs shown in My Sample after sample registration.
  2. Use the correct template for the selected technique.
  3. If one sample has multiple files, repeat the same Sample ID in multiple rows, one row per file.
  4. Keep uploaded file names exactly the same as the file names entered in the template.
  5. Generate the MD5 checksum only after the final file or ZIP is ready.
  6. Use NA for required fields that are genuinely not applicable.

Calculate MD5 Checksum First

Complete the MD5 checksum section before registering the experiment. Copy only the checksum value for the exact final file that will be uploaded.

Quality Check

Do not use local sample names where IMDA expects Sample IDs. Do not rename, delete, or reorder template columns. Confirm that the technique, Study ID, Sample ID, data-file name, and MD5 checksum describe the same final file.

docs.title: Submit and Continue
docs.text:
1. Download the correct MS or NMR template.
  2. Fill it using IMDA Sample IDs, exact final file names, and matching MD5 checksums.
  3. Upload the compulsory metabolite/compound result file.
  4. Upload the completed MS or NMR template.
  5. Click Submit, then continue to FTP File Uploads.
Next: FTP File Uploads ↓

docs.title: FTP File Uploads
docs.text: Use the FTP details shown in the IMDA portal to upload your prepared data files. Keep the password private and do not share screenshots that show the real password.

docs.title: Step 1: Get FTP Login and Folder Details
docs.text: First open FTP Files Upload in the IMDA sidebar. This page gives the FTP login details and shows which project/study folder must be used for the selected study.

docs.title: What to Check on the FTP Page
docs.text:
Portal Item What the User Should Do Hostname Copy this into the Host field in FileZilla or another FTP client. Username Copy this into the Username field. Password Copy this into the Password field. Do not share it in email, screenshots, or documents. Study ID After submitting the experiment form and template, open this dropdown and select the correct temporary Study ID, such as TEMP_IMS_XX. Project Folder After the temporary Study ID is selected, the portal displays its related Project Folder, such as TEMP_IMP_XX. Open this folder first in the FTP client. Study Folder The portal also displays the related Study Folder, such as TEMP_IMS_XX. Open this folder inside the Project Folder and upload the data files there.

Use the Folder Names Shown in the Portal

Complete Register Experiment first. On the FTP page, select the correct temporary Study ID from the dropdown. IMDA will then display the matching temporary Project Folder and Study Folder created for that submission. Use these exact folder names in the FTP client; do not guess, rename, or create the folders manually.

docs.title: Step 2: Upload Files in FileZilla
docs.text: Use FileZilla to connect to the IMDA FTP server and transfer the final prepared files into the correct Study Folder.

docs.title: FileZilla Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open FileZilla or another FTP client.
  2. Enter the Host, Username, and Password exactly as shown in the IMDA FTP page.
  3. If a port is provided, enter it in the Port field. Otherwise, leave the port blank and connect normally.
  4. Open the Project Folder shown in the portal.
  5. Open the Study Folder shown under that project.
  6. Upload the final ZIP/raw data files into the study folder.
  7. After upload, continue to Validate Files in this SOP.

Before Upload

Generate the MD5 checksum after the final ZIP file is ready. Do not rename, edit, or recompress the file after MD5 generation, because the checksum will change.

After upload, continue to Validate Files. On that page, use Map Uploaded Files from the IMDA sidebar to check and validate the uploaded files.

Next: Validate Files ↓

docs.title: Login / Register
docs.text: Register and log in before starting a data submission.

docs.title: Where to Login or Register
docs.text:
Open the IMDA portal and use the top-right links to access Login or User Registration. To log in, click Login, enter the registered username and password, complete the reCAPTCHA, and click Login.

Option User Action Purpose User Registration Open User Registration. Creates the account required for data submission. Login Open Login. Starts an authenticated session for submission and dashboard access. Submit Open Submit Data after login. Opens the new data submission workflow.

docs.title: User Registration Form
docs.text:
Fill all mandatory fields marked with an asterisk. Use an active email address because account activation and IMDA communication will go to this email. Scroll inside the image box to view the full form.

After registration, check the registered email for the account activation link. If login fails because the account is not active, use Resend activation link to admin on the login page.

docs.title: Edit Profile
docs.text:
After login, users can open Profile from the top menu. Click Edit Profile to update details such as name, email, organization, designation, ORCID, and country when corrections are needed.

Before Starting Submission

Make sure the user profile has the correct full name, email address, organization name, designation, and country. These details help IMDA identify the submitter and contact the right person if clarification is needed.

docs.title: After Login: User Dashboard
docs.text:
After login, the dashboard is the main page where users can check their submitted data and continue the submission workflow.

Next: Project ↓

docs.title: Validate Files
docs.text: After FTP upload, open Map Uploaded Files from the IMDA sidebar to validate the files. This step checks whether uploaded files are visible for the correct study and whether each file is ready for final submission.

docs.title: What This Page Shows
docs.text: Item What It Means Study ID The study where the uploaded files are listed. Check that you are working under the correct study. FTP Run ID The upload run generated by IMDA for each uploaded file. File Name The file detected from FTP upload. Confirm that the name matches the file name used in the experiment template. Status Shows whether the uploaded file is mapped and accepted. If it remains Unmapped, check the file name and uploaded file details. Validate All Files For This Study Click this button after checking all files for that study.

docs.title: Validation Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open Map Uploaded Files from the left sidebar.
  2. Find the correct Study ID.
  3. Check that every expected uploaded file is listed.
  4. Confirm the file names match the experiment template and MD5 checksum information.
  5. Click Validate All Files For This Study.
  6. Check the Status column. When the file details are correct, the status should change from Unmapped to OK.

If the Status Stays Unmapped

Check whether the uploaded file name matches the experiment template exactly. Also confirm that the file was uploaded into the correct study folder in FTP. Correct the issue, then validate again.

Before Moving to Submitted Data

Do not move to final submission if expected files are missing, mapped to the wrong study, or still showing Unmapped.

Next: Submitted Data ↓

docs.title: MD5 Checksum
docs.text:
Generate MD5 checksums before uploading data files. The checksum works like a file fingerprint and helps IMDA confirm that the uploaded file is the same as the file on your computer.

Access the Tool: Calculate MD5Checksum for Your Files Here.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Keep all final data files in a single folder. Download the script for Windows, macOS, or Linux and save the downloaded script in the same folder.
  2. Run the script as described in the instructions shown on the IMDA MD5 tool page. Confirm that it generates md5sum.txt, then copy each checksum into the Md5checksum column for the matching file row in the MS or NMR experiment template.

Checksum Rules

Enter MD5 checksum values in lowercase and make sure each checksum corresponds to the exact ZIP file uploaded.

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
sample_data.zip  8b1a9953c4611296a827abf8c47804d7
sample_data_02.zip  6f5902ac237024bdd0c176cb93063dc4
sample_data_03.mzML  098f6bcd4621d373cade4e832627b4f6

Each line shows the exact data-file name followed by its matching 32-character MD5 checksum. Enter each checksum in the experiment-template row for the same file name.

Common Mistakes

Generate the checksum after the final ZIP file is ready. If you rename, edit, re-zip, or replace a file, generate the checksum again.

Next: Experiment ↓

docs.title: Reviewer Access URL
docs.text: Use the reviewer access URL to share a completed controlled-access or managed-access study with journal reviewers before public release.

docs.title: When to Generate the Link
docs.text: For a controlled-access or managed-access study, generate the reviewer link only after the study is fully submitted and the uploaded files are validated. The Activate Now option appears in the Reviewer Access column for a completed study.

docs.title: Data Availability Statement
docs.text:
Indian Metabolome Data Archive (IMDA)

The data are available at the Indian Metabolome Data Archive (IMDA) of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC), https://ibdc.dbtindia.gov.in/imda/home, with IBDC Project accession no. IMP_XXXXXX and Study accession no. IMS_XXXXXX.

Replace IMP_XXXXXX and IMS_XXXXXX with the permanent accession numbers assigned to the submitted project and study.

docs.title: Generate and Share the Link
docs.text:
1. Open Submitted Data or the completed study list.
  2. Find the required study row.
  3. Click Activate Now under Reviewer Access.
  4. On the URLs to Share Study Records page, click Copy.
  5. Share the copied link only with the intended journal reviewer, editor, or collaborator.

Common Mistakes

Confirm the correct study before sharing the reviewer link. Do not share the link publicly or with unintended users.

docs.title: Access Limit
docs.text:
• Maximum access: 5 people at a time.
  • Link validity: 24 hours.
  • Generate a new link if the previous link expires.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text: Use Register Sample from the left sidebar. Select the correct Study ID, enter the source and organism details, and upload the completed sample template.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Select Study* Study ID to which these samples belong. Choose the correct study before uploading the template. Source* Biological material or source from which the sample came, such as tissue, cell line, biofluid, plant part, culture, or environmental source. Select the closest available controlled term. Avoid local abbreviations. Organism Name* Scientific organism name. Use binomial name, for example Homo sapiens or Oryza sativa. Taxonomy ID* NCBI taxonomy number fetched by the system. Check that the number matches the organism name. Additional Information Relevant sample characteristics, such as organism part, cell type, disease or condition, treatment, collection site, control status, or quality-control status. Use clear and consistent terms. Enter NA only when the information genuinely does not apply. Sample File Template* Completed sample Excel template. Do not change column names in the template.

docs.title: Sample Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the Sample file template, fill one row for each sample, and upload the completed Excel file in Sample File Template. Do not rename, delete, or reorder its columns.

Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample Name Unique sample identifier used by the submitter. Use the same name later in the MS or NMR experiment template. Sample Type Role or material type, such as experimental sample, control, quality-control sample, standard, pooled sample, plasma, serum, tissue, extract, culture, or cell line, as appropriate. Sample Preparation Protocol Short description of how the sample was prepared before extraction or analysis. Extraction Protocol Solvent, method, or protocol used to extract metabolites from the sample. Experimental Condition (Treated/Untreated, Healthy/Diseased, Others) Study factor or condition that distinguishes groups, such as treated, untreated, control, diseased, healthy, exposed, dose group, or time point. Use the same terms for samples in the same group. Time of treatment Treatment duration or collection time point, such as 0 h, 24 h, 7 days, or NA if not applicable. Variant/Variety Strain, cultivar, variety, genotype, breed, or variant where applicable. Use NA if not applicable. Gender Male, female, pooled, mixed, not recorded, or NA depending on the sample type. Age Age of organism or subject, including unit where possible, such as 8 weeks, 45 days, adult, or NA. Replicates Replicate number or group, such as biological replicate 1, technical replicate 2, R1, R2, R3, or pooled. Keep biological and technical replicates distinguishable. Storage Conditions How the sample was stored before analysis, such as -80°C, liquid nitrogen, 4°C, room temperature, or NA. Number of files per sample Exact number of raw/processed data files that belong to that sample. This number should match the files uploaded later.

After template submission, IMDA generates Sample IDs. Use these IDs in the experiment template to link each analytical measurement and data file to the correct sample.

Required Sample Context

Each sample should clearly connect to one study and one source. Check the study, sample name, organism name, taxonomy ID, and source before submitting.

docs.title: Submit and Continue
docs.text:
1. Download and complete the sample file template.
  2. Upload it using Choose File.
  3. Click Submit to register sample metadata.
  4. Open My Sample and keep the generated Sample IDs for the experiment template.

Quality Check

Confirm that sample names are unique, the selected Study ID is correct, the taxonomy ID matches the organism, and the number of files per sample is exact. Do not change template headers or use NA for information that is available.

Next: MD5 Checksum ↓

docs.title: Study
docs.text:
Use Register Study from the left sidebar and select the correct Project ID. A study is a specific scientific investigation or dataset within a project.

Temporary Study ID

After submitting this form, IMDA will assign a temporary Study ID in the format TEMP_IMS_XX.

docs.title: Study Details
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Descriptive title of the specific investigation or dataset. Include the organism or source, condition, and analytical approach where possible. The title should agree with the related manuscript title when applicable. Study Type* Analytical technique, such as Mass Spectrometry (MS) or Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Select the technique used to generate the submitted data. Data Type / Summary Study design or data type, such as targeted, semi-targeted, or untargeted, plus a concise scientific summary. Explain the objective, samples, comparison or treatment, analytical method, and data generated in 3-5 clear sentences. Keywords Terms that describe the study and help users find it. Use 3-8 specific terms covering the organism, disease or condition, sample type, analytical method, and metabolite class where relevant. Release Date* Date on which the data can become publicly available. Use the required portal date format. Publication / Approval DOI, PubMed ID, manuscript status, IEC/IBSC approval, or institutional approval number. Enter official numbers exactly as issued. If not available, use the portal's allowed option.

docs.title: Submit and Continue
docs.text:
1. Confirm the selected Project ID.
  2. Complete the study details and author list.
  3. Click Submit to register the study.
  4. Keep the temporary Study ID and select it when registering samples, experiments, and files.

Quality Check

Do not repeat the project title unless it accurately describes this specific study. Confirm that the summary, keywords, study type, data type, release date, and contributor details describe the same investigation.

Next: Sample ↓

docs.title: Submitted Data
docs.text: Use Submitted Data to check whether your study has been submitted, reviewed, corrected, or released.

docs.title: Tracking Your Study
docs.text:
1. Open Submitted Data from the IMDA sidebar.
  2. Review the table of submitted files for the selected project and study.
  3. Check the Status column for each file.
  4. A status of OK means the file was validated and submitted successfully.
  5. If any expected file is missing or does not show OK, return to Validate Files and validate again.
Status Meaning Action Required OK File was validated and submitted successfully. No action needed for that file. Unmapped File is uploaded but not fully mapped or validated. Go back to Validate Files, check file names and mapping, then validate again. Missing file Expected file is not visible in Submitted Data. Check the FTP upload folder and upload the file again if needed.

After Submission

Use this page to review files submitted across your IMDA projects and studies. IMDA may contact the registered email if any correction is required.

docs.title: Corrections After Submission
docs.text:
Use Edit File Data only when study details or uploaded files need correction before final submit/check, or when IMDA asks for a correction.

Submission Status Edit Button Status Required Action Pre-Submission Active Click the edit option for the relevant row. Post-Submission Disabled or hidden Contact IMDA support to request temporary edit access.

Common edit actions include:

  • Edit Project / Study / Sample Details: Correct project, study, or sample information before final submit/check.
  • Edit Upload Run: Replace corrupted or incorrect raw data files.
  • Edit Metabolite / Compound File: Replace the processed metabolite summary file.

docs.title: Edit Upload Run
docs.text:
Use Edit Upload Run when a raw data file needs correction or replacement.

Field What to Enter Study Select the study linked to the uploaded run. FTP Filename Select the uploaded file that needs correction. MD5 Checksum Enter the corrected lowercase checksum for the replacement file.

docs.title: Edit Metabolite / Compound File
docs.text:
Use this option when the processed metabolite or compound file needs to be replaced.

Field What to Enter Study Select the study linked to the processed file. Compound Document Upload the corrected metabolite or compound file.

docs.title: Controlled Vocabulary Updates
docs.text:
Use Browse Lists to check whether an organism, source, or MS/NMR instrument name is already available in IMDA. If the required name is missing, use Update List to request it.

Browse List What to Check MS Instrument Confirm whether the required mass spectrometry instrument already exists. NMR Instrument Confirm whether the required NMR instrument already exists. Source / Organism Terms Use existing portal terms wherever possible.

docs.title: Update List
docs.text:
Request a new list value only when the required value is not already available.

Field What to Enter List Type Select the category to update, such as MS instrument, NMR instrument, organism, or source. Name / Value Enter the exact term to be added.

docs.title: Support and Citation
docs.text:
Item Guidance Repository Indian Metabolome Data Archive (IMDA) of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC). Project ID Use the assigned IMP_xxxxxx ID. Study ID Use the assigned IMS_xxxxxx ID. Support Email Contact imda.support@ibdc.rcb.res.in for assistance.

Common Mistakes

Do not assume the submission is complete only because files were uploaded. Check the status in Submitted Data and respond quickly if IMDA requests corrections.

Next: Reviewer Access URL ↓
